content: 1. If a child has experienced diarrhea for more than 14 days, was the condition managed appropriately? Did the healthcare worker provide guidance on when to bring the child back for follow-up care? 2. Ask the caregiver: What is the primary source of drinking water for your household members? Indicate Yes for the main water source: Piped water into the dwelling, yard, or plot Public tap or standpipe Protected well, spring, or rainwater harvesting Unprotected well, spring, or rainwater harvesting Bottled water, sachet water, or water transported by cart, drum, or tanker truck Surface water (e.g., river, dam, lake, pond, stream, canal, irrigation channel) 3. If the main water source is not on the premises, how long does it take to fetch water, including the round trip? Do you treat your water to make it safer for drinking? If so, what methods do you use? 4. What type of toilet facility does your household typically use? Indicate Yes for the one used: Flush toilet connected to a piped sewer system, septic tank, or pit latrine Flush toilet to an unknown location Flush toilet to an open drain or elsewhere Ventilated improved latrine or simple pit latrine with a slab Composting toilet Pit latrine without a slab, open pit, bucket latrine, or hanging toilet 5. Do you share this toilet facility with other households? If yes, how many households share it? When your child last passed stools, how were they disposed of? Options include: Child used a toilet/latrine Stools were put or rinsed into a toilet/latrine Stools were put or rinsed into a drain or ditch Stools were thrown into garbage Stools were buried Stools were left in the open Other (please specify) 6. Are soap and water currently available at your handwashing facilities? 7. Did a healthcare worker counsel you on practices to reduce the risk of waterborne diseases? These practices may include: Upgrading to a piped or protected water source Safely transporting and storing water Properly disinfecting water (e.g., boiling) Washing hands before preparing food and eating Washing hands with soap Washing hands before touching the child 8. For children with cough or difficulty breathing, did the healthcare worker: Ask if the child had a cough or wheezing? Ask how long the child had been coughing or wheezing? Provide a trial of an inhaled puffer or nebulizer? Advise on using an inhaled puffer at home for five days or returning for nebulizer use? Refer the child for further assessment of tuberculosis or asthma if symptoms persisted for more than 14 days? Prescribe antibiotics, and if so, explain why they were given and when to return for follow-up? 9. Does anyone in your household engage in activities that contribute to indoor air pollution, such as smoking or using wood, charcoal, dung, or kerosene for cooking or heating? Did the healthcare worker provide advice on reducing indoor air pollution, such as: Eliminating indoor smoking Changing cooking fuel Cooking outdoors Improving household ventilation Switching to alternative lighting sources? 10. For children with fever, did the healthcare worker: Ask how many days the child had a fever? Test for malaria, and if positive, prescribe antimalarial medication? Provide advice on preventing malaria and when to return for follow-up? 11. For children with skin infections, ear pain/discharge, sore throat, or red/sticky eyes, did the healthcare worker prescribe antibiotics and explain their use? 12. For children with developmental or chronic health problems (e.g., visual or hearing impairments, cerebral palsy, ADHD, autism, cleft lip/palate, spina bifida, Down syndrome), did the healthcare worker: Prescribe antiretroviral therapy or co-trimoxazole prophylaxis if HIV-positive? Assess feeding and provide counseling on nutrition? Offer advice on home care and follow-up visits? Refer the child for higher-level assessment or management? 13. For injuries, abuse, or neglect, did the healthcare worker ask about recent injuries requiring medical attention? What was the cause of the injury (e.g., road traffic accident, fall, blunt trauma, burn, poisoning, electric shock, water-related, animal or human bite)? What was the nature of the injury (e.g., fracture, laceration, joint dislocation, contusion)? Did the healthcare worker provide counseling on injury prevention? 14. For early child development, did the healthcare worker ask about developmental concerns or refer the child for further assessment? Did they counsel on promoting development through activities like reading, playing, and communication? Did they emphasize the importance of playgroups and early education? 15. Did the healthcare worker review the child’s health records and re-examine the child after the caregiver interview? Were findings from the re-examination consistent with the case records?
